transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-02
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 min
Attendees: Ava Patel (Redwood AE); Liam Chen (Redwood SE); Maria Gonzales (SentinelQ - Head of ML); Rajiv Menon (SentinelQ - Platform); Sofia Ruiz (SentinelQ - Security)

Auto Summary:
SentinelQ is evaluating porting their production chat and summarization pipelines off a hosted OpenAI + vLLM sidecar to a unified vendor. Primary concerns: maintaining eval parity (quality + hallucination rates), meeting p95 latency < 350ms for short chats, and data residency/SOC2 controls for PII. They asked about Redwood's hosted vs dedicated vs private options and how to run parity benchmarks using TGI/vLLM artifacts. Next steps: pricing + SLAs, benchmark plan, sample prompts, security docs.

Topics (auto-tag): migration, eval parity, hosting modes, benchmarks, security, quantization

Action items (auto): see metadata list above

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ava Patel: Hey everyone thanks for carving out time, um, quick intros — I'm Ava, AE at Redwood — Liam is our SE — and who do we have on the Sentinal — SentinelQ side?
[00:07] Maria Gonzales: Hey Ava, Maria here, head of ML, I run model selection and evaluation — Rajiv in infra and Sofia handles security — thanks for making time.
[00:14] Ava Patel: Great. Goal for today's call is discovery — understand your current stack, blockers, and what a successful port looks like. Liam will dive into technical fit.
[00:22] Rajiv Menon: For context, we run chat + long form summarization. Currently using OpenAI hosted for generation and a vLLM sidecar on prem for lower-latency local calls. We've got traffic pattern: steady, about 6k tokens/min at peak for user-facing chat, plus nightly batch summarization.
[00:38] Liam Chen: Thanks — quick clarifying question, when you say vLLM sidecar, is that the internal inferencing with KV cache pinned to the app or a separate service?
[00:45] Rajiv Menon: Separate service, yeah. vLLM on a couple of A100s, runs TGI forks for local requests to reduce cost for internal workload. The problem is orchestration complexity and drift with OpenAI outputs — our prod outputs don't always match OpenAI completions which causes UX regressions.
[01:05] Maria Gonzales: Exactly — eval parity is the kicker — we can't have different hallucination profiles between OpenAI and our local models. Our product team measures F1 on intent extraction and hallucination rate on a 2k prompt eval set.
[01:18] Ava Patel: Totally — so two big threads: 1) portability/parity (we'll need to reproduce your OpenAI baseline quality) and 2) operational fit (latency, cost, and security). We support hosted API, dedicated GPU pools, and private VPC/on-prem. Which of those are you leaning toward?
[01:33] Sofia Ruiz: Security with compliance is non-negotiable — SOC2, and we need KMS/HSM integration plus audit logs. Ideally a VPC option but depends on cost.
[01:41] Rajiv Menon: From infra we'll want predictability — dedicated capacity is attractive if we can cap costs and keep throughput guarantees.
[01:48] Liam Chen: Understood. On parity: our approach is twofold — first, an eval parity run using your 2k prompt set against candidate open models and the model version you use with OpenAI; second, we run a token-level diff and ngram hallucination detection to highlight behavioral mismatches. We can include TGI/vLLM runner compatibility in our tests.
[02:10] Maria Gonzales: Can you run our evals on hosted Redwood or do we need a private env? We can't send PII out.
[02:16] Ava Patel: If it contains PII, we recommend either dedicated with customer data isolation or our private deployment. For the initial parity we can run a de-identified subset on hosted to speed things up, and then repeat in a private env for full verification.
[02:29] Maria Gonzales: That makes sense. How do you handle model variants and rollouts? We do canary tests now but it's fragile.
[02:35] Liam Chen: We expose rollouts and canary routing in the Console — you can pin model versions, run A/B with traffic split, and automatic fallback to a smaller model if the primary is degraded. We also provide token-level cost breakdowns and latency dashboards.
[02:50] Rajiv Menon: Latency requirement — we aim for p95 under 350ms for single-turn chats ~ up to 128 tokens. Nightly summarization batch is not latency sensitive. Does Redwood hit those numbers on similar models?
[03:01] Liam Chen: For short sequences on dedicated NVIDIA A100 or newer Gaudi-type instances we typically see p95 in the 200–400ms range depending on batch settings and KV cache warmness. Our Smart batching tries to keep latency SLOs while increasing throughput. For hosted customers we publish performance profiles per model.
[03:20] Maria Gonzales: And cost? Right now OpenAI is expensive at scale. We're hoping Redwood reduces unit cost but not at the expense of quality.
[03:27] Ava Patel: Cost is a lever — dedicated + quantization + KV caching + batching can cut per-token costs significantly. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles and batching configs per workload. We'll include some modeled estimates in the pricing doc.
[03:41] Sofia Ruiz: On the security side — can Redwood bring a private control plane for Private deployments? We need customer-managed KMS and audit retention options.
[03:50] Liam Chen: Yes, Private runs can be deployed with a customer-managed control plane in a VPC and integrate with KMS/HSM. We provide audit logs and RBAC integrations (SSO/SAML). For SOC2, we share the report under NDA — we'll add that to the doc pack.
[04:04] Maria Gonzales: Good. One practical question — how do you handle tokenizer differences? We occasionally see tokenization mismatches between OpenAI tokenizer and TGI forks. That affects billing and output forms.
[04:15] Liam Chen: We can normalize tokenization by running the same tokenizer used by your OpenAI model—if you share the model identifier we try to match tokenization behavior, and we include prefix normalization and canonicalization layers. There are edge cases but we document diffs in the parity report.
[04:30] Rajiv Menon: For the evals, we want to prioritize examples where OpenAI currently out-performs our in-house vLLM. Can Redwood reproduce OpenAI completions or at least the top-k behavior?
[04:40] Liam Chen: Reproduce exactly is hard if OpenAI uses proprietary tweaks, but we can achieve behavioral parity across metrics you care about — hallucination, instruction-following, safety checks. We'll iterate with model selection + prompt engineering and measure delta on your 2k suite.
[04:58] Maria Gonzales: What about model families? Do you recommend open models (Llama-style) or Redwood-curated variants?
[05:05] Ava Patel: We curate model variants with performance profiles. For many customers, a curated open model plus quantization and Redwood runtime yields the best cost/latency tradeoff. For some use cases the hosted OpenAI parity is achieved faster via larger open models running on Dedicated. We'll suggest candidates after we see your eval set.
[05:23] Rajiv Menon: Ok, on networking — if we go Dedicated in a cloud region, what are the egress/residency considerations? We have EU data residency needs for some customers.
[05:31] Ava Patel: We have regions in US and EU; Dedicated capacity can be provisioned in EU regions for residency. Private deployments in your VPC give full control. We'll include region options in the pricing doc.
[05:41] Sofia Ruiz: Any contract minimums for Dedicated? Procurement will want to know annual commit levels.
[05:46] Ava Patel: Typical minimums depend on GPU counts and term — we'll provide a few standard commitment tiers in the proposal. You can start with a pilot to validate parity with a small commit.
[05:55] Maria Gonzales: Pilot — good. For the pilot we want a reproducible benchmark harness. Does Redwood provide runners for vLLM/TGI so we can compare apples to apples?
[06:03] Liam Chen: Yes, our benchmarking harness supports running workloads on vLLM and TGI forks plus Redwood's runtime and OpenAI. We'll share scripts that run a 2k prompt set, compute BLEU/ROUGE/F1/hallucination metrics, and produce a behavior diff. The idea is to use identical prompts, temperature, top-k/pp settings to minimize confounding variables.
[06:22] Maria Gonzales: Perfect. Are there any known incompatibilities with the TGI forks we should watch for?
[06:27] Liam Chen: Mostly around newer attention kernels and kv cache persistence across restarts. Also quantization artifacts at 4-bit may change subtle generation patterns. We'll surface those in the parity report.
[06:38] Rajiv Menon: For monitoring, do we get traces per request? We need to be able to trace a user request from ingress to model response and see model-level timings.
[06:47] Liam Chen: Console includes per-route tracing hooks and token-level timing. We can also forward traces to your existing observability backend (Datadog/Prometheus).
[06:55] Sofia Ruiz: On compliance, our legal team will ask about data retention and deletion. Can logs be configured to redact PII and be retained only for X days?
[07:04] Liam Chen: Yes, retention policies are configurable; redaction and pseudonymization can be applied. For Private deployments you control logs in your VPC.
[07:12] Maria Gonzales: Great. Quick budget note — procurement loves hard numbers. Can you give a rough cost delta vs our current spend? We're trying to cut per-token costs by ~40% without raising latency.
[07:23] Ava Patel: We'll model a couple of scenarios: hosted replacement, dedicated with reserved capacity, and private. We'll include estimated savings assuming quantization and caching gains. Exact numbers will depend on traffic distribution and model choices.
[07:37] Rajiv Menon: How long does a typical migration to Dedicated look like? From pilot to full cutover?
[07:42] Ava Patel: Pilot to canary typically 4–8 weeks depending on eval cycles; full production cutover often 8–16 weeks for mature teams. We'll propose a phased plan in the follow-up.
[07:54] Maria Gonzales: Can you walk briefly through a sample parity result so we know what to expect in the report?
[07:59] Liam Chen: Sure — we'll show side-by-side completions, token-level diffs, hallucination flags, and metric deltas. We'll also include suggested prompt tweaks and a recommended model/version plus quantization profile.
[08:11] Maria Gonzales: What if we find a 5–7% degradation in a safety metric — are there guardrails to fallback to OpenAI?
[08:18] Liam Chen: Yes, routing policies can fallback to OpenAI or another variant automatically when quality dips or latency spikes. That can be a transitional safety net.
[08:27] Rajiv Menon: On the technical side, what's the integration effort? We have an internal service that calls OpenAI via an adapter. How much work to switch to Redwood API?
[08:36] Liam Chen: The Redwood API is REST/SDK compatible for generation and embeddings. For many customers it's a small change — swap endpoints, do a few config changes around model names. We also provide client libraries and quickstart templates.
[08:49] Maria Gonzales: Do you have customers who've done this exact 'OpenAI+vLLM' consolidation? Any case studies?
[08:55] Ava Patel: Yes, we can share a case (we'll include a redacted deck) where a fintech customer consolidated from mixed providers to Dedicated Redwood capacity and achieved parity with 30% cost reduction. We'll add that link.
[09:07] Sofia Ruiz: About legal — we'll want indemnity language and security addendum. Is that standard?
[09:12] Ava Patel: We provide a security addendum and standard indemnity clauses; legal will send templates and we can negotiate.
[09:19] Maria Gonzales: Ok I want to pivot to benchmarking specifics — our 2k suite has ~15% prompts that are multi-turn. Do you support multi-turn KV cache tests that simulate chat history?
[09:29] Liam Chen: Yes, the harness supports multi-turn sequences and warm cache scenarios to emulate chat. We'll include p50/p95/p99 metrics with cold and warm cache runs.
[09:38] Rajiv Menon: For the pilot, we'll need a short SLA on response time for the test to be meaningful. Can Redwood provide temporary SLA for pilot?
[09:45] Ava Patel: We can do a pilot-level SLO documented in the pilot agreement; for production SLA's those are part of Dedicated contracts.
[09:50] Maria Gonzales: Good. Any risks we should be aware of?
[09:54] Liam Chen: Main risks: 1) exact tokenization/model differences when matching OpenAI, 2) quantization causing subtle quality regression, 3) initial engineering effort to run parity and integrate routing — all manageable with an iterative pilot.
[10:06] Maria Gonzales: Sounds reasonable. On hosting — for Private deployment we might want on-prem. How heavy is the on-prem package?
[10:13] Liam Chen: On-prem is heavier — it includes the private control plane, orchestration components, and a small ops runbook. We usually recommend VPC first unless there's air-gapped requirement.
[10:23] Rajiv Menon: If we do VPC private deploy, how is software updated? We don't want surprise behavior changes during a business-critical rollout.
[10:30] Liam Chen: Updates are controlled by you — you approve control-plane updates. For hosted and dedicated we manage updates but provide release notes and canary windows.
[10:38] Sofia Ruiz: What's the escalation path if we hit production regressions post-cutover?
[10:43] Ava Patel: We assign a CSM and an SE for escalation; Dedicated comes with higher support SLAs. We'll outline support tiers in the proposal.
[10:51] Maria Gonzales: Ok this has been super helpful. A few clarifying points for the follow-up: 1) include a recommended model shortlist and expected cost/latency profiles, 2) sample parity report template, 3) security whitepaper and SOC2 under NDA, 4) pilot statement of work.
[11:05] Ava Patel: Absolutely — we'll send all that. Liam, anything to add?
[11:09] Liam Chen: I'll draft the benchmark plan and include runner scripts for vLLM/TGI/OpenAI comparators. Also will surface known TGI kv-cache caveats in writing.
[11:19] Maria Gonzales: Perfect. Timeline — we aim to start pilot by mid-April. Any blockers from Redwood side?
[11:26] Ava Patel: No blockers — we'll turn docs around within a few days. We'll align schedules for the week of April 13 for a hands-on eval.
[11:33] Sofia Ruiz: Please also include contact for security review calls — our security lead might want a deep dive.
[11:39] Ava Patel: We'll include a proposed slot for a security deep-dive next week.
[11:44] Rajiv Menon: One last thing — can Redwood's runtime export token-level cost traces so we can reconcile bill vs infra usage?
[11:51] Liam Chen: Yes, token-level traces and cost breakdown per request are available in the Console and via APIs.
[11:56] Maria Gonzales: Thanks everyone — wrap up?
[11:59] Ava Patel: Quick recap: 1) We'll deliver pricing + region options + SLA tiers; 2) Liam sends benchmark plan and runner scripts; 3) customer shares 2k prompt set (de-identified where needed); 4) schedule pilot week of Apr 13. Action items and owners noted in follow-up.
[12:19] Maria Gonzales: Thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
